definition: Dubious means doubtful, of uncertain quality.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word dubious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know dubious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Even nine-year-old Tess found the coupon's promise of a free island vacation dubious.
Iffy is a shrug - the picnic might still happen, but take an umbrella; dubious goes further, meaning the doubt has real teeth.
Implausible sits above dubious on the ladder: a dubious claim raises eyebrows, while an implausible one collides head-on with common sense.

Questionable is doubt at its mildest and most polite: the claim invites a second look, and the question is still open. Dubious has already leaned - the eyebrow is up, and believing feels unwise. A questionable receipt gets checked; a dubious one gets checked by someone frowning.

Suspect means already sitting under a cloud - suspicion has hardened into a working assumption that something is wrong, often dishonestly so. Dubious is a stage earlier and broader: quality or truth in real doubt, but no accusation yet. Results can be dubious through sloppiness; they turn suspect when someone may have cooked them.

By the final lap her lead was indubitable, and even the rival coaches stopped checking their stopwatches.
Dubious means doubtful, of uncertain quality.
The convertible gleamed, but its history was dubious: 40,000 miles on the dial, three owners in two years, and a service record that skipped 2019 entirely.
Nothing proved the odometer lied; everything invited you to wonder.
Dubious captures a claim that invites doubt on its face: the mileage may be true, but three owners and a missing year make believing it feel unwise.
Notice the word works two ways - the buyers were dubious (they felt the doubt), and the mileage was dubious (it caused the doubt).
Dubious carries a raised eyebrow: the claim, prize, or honor already smells off.
Unverified, its no-judgment cousin in this unit, just means unchecked - say dubious only when doubt has actually set in.
And it runs both directions: you can be dubious about a scheme, or the scheme itself can be dubious.
